thread:
alex: FYI support ticket from ACME - big p99 spike after last runtime rollout. Customers seeing 4-6s p99 on short prompts. filing here to coordinate triage

maria: which rollout? canary or full? any correlating deploy logs?

alex: deploy-bot shows rollout finished ~1h ago (canary->stable promoted). thread_ts: 6191108000 in deploy logs. symptoms: p50 ok, p95 up ~200ms, p99 up multiple seconds.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T09:12Z: runtime v3.4.1 promoted from canary to stable. change: kernel-scheduler tweak + auth-client bump.

ken: auth-client bump stands out. last time auth sync change caused bursts when token refreshs became sync. can we surface auth latencies?

sri: good call. ingest-bot, do we have auth call histograms around 09:12-09:40?

ingest-bot: auth.latency.histogram (09:00-10:00): p50=15ms, p95=180ms, p99=1.9s. spike aligns w/ rollout.

maria: that 1.9s p99 for auth is probably the backpressure source. runtime holds worker while waiting for auth, causing tail queueing. need quick mitigation: route traffic to previous runtime variant or enable auth circuit-breaker.

oncall: can we do a partial rollback for only auth-client? not trivial. easier: routing fallback to cohort that stayed on older runtime. we can route 25% -> previous until fix.

alex: ops: please trigger routing revert. samira, can you prepare a scoped rollback if needed?

samira: starting traffic split rollback now. command: `rbctl promote --from runtime-v3.3.9 --to runtime-v3.4.1 --split 75` (this is for reference, doing actual change via console).

ken: also let's enable debug logging on auth client for a small cohort so we can capture stack traces without noise. add env: AUTH_CLIENT_DEBUG=true for 5% sample.

sri: adding probe requests to reproduce: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` run 200 parallel short calls and sample latency distribution. include header `X-Redwood-Trial:canary-test` to hit canary cohort.

alex: capturing a few slow traces from support ticket: Attached snippet (stack condensed):
```
auth_client::refresh_token() waiting on remote OIDC (connection timeout 1200ms)
runtime::request_executor waiting on auth future -> hold worker -> queue++
```

maria: looks like auth refreshes are doing blocking network with a bad timeout. previous version used async non-blocking path. the bump probably reverted to sync path inadvertently.

samira: we've applied traffic split: 30% -> v3.3.9, 70% -> v3.4.1. early telemetry shows p99 dropping from ~4.8s -> ~1.6s in the 30% cohort. overall p99 trending down.

oncall: opening customer comms: psa to affected tenants and ETA for fix.

ken: next steps: 1) short-term routing split (done), 2) enable auth circuit-breaker/timeout to 300ms in runtime to fail-fast and fallback to lightweight check, 3) revert the auth-client change on stable or hotpatch to async path. which of 2/3 can we ship fastest?

sri: 2 is config-only and can be toggled via feature flags. I can push flag now: `featurectl set runtime.auth.failfast_timeout_ms=300` for prod.

alex: please push flag and monitor. Also collect traces for any requests that hit failfast - we need to understand fallout.

samira: flag set. monitoring: auth p99 dropped to ~420ms within 5m. runtime p99 now ~900ms. still above baseline but much better.

maria: good. schedule a rollback of the auth-client bump in the next maintenance window if hotpatch isn't possible. also add a canary test that simulates token refresh storms during rollout.

ken: add repro steps to the changelist so future rollouts run token-refresh load test: script in CI `ci/canary/token_refresh_storm.sh` - run 1k refreshes concurrently against canary.

alex: support ticket updated with mitigation + workaround: route to older runtime or set failfast flag. customer accepted workaround for now.

samira: I'll prepare a hotfix to restore async path. want to run it as a canary + monitor auth.latency histogram and runtime.queue_depth metric.

ingest-bot: metric snapshots: pre-fix runtime.queue_depth.p99=4 -> after split & flag 2 -> 1. runtime.auth.latency.p99 fell from 1.9s -> 0.42s.

alex: thanks everyone. keep this thread updated with any anomalies. we'll close once hotfix roll is in stable and p99 back to baseline for 30m. :thumbsup:
